mainTopic: End of פרק כל הגט and the opening of פרק השולח: how and until when a husband can cancel a גט he sent, and which words count as cancelling it
overview: The amud opens with the end of פרק כל הגט. The word יפרי is explained as heavy rain loosening things that are fitted tightly together, with three examples that each go further than the last. After the הדרן, פרק השולח begins with a משנה. A husband who sent a גט can cancel it by telling the שליח or his wife, in person or through another שליח, as long as the גט has not reached her hand. The משנה also says that people once cancelled a גט before a בית דין somewhere else, and רבן גמליאל הזקן stopped this מפני תיקון העולם. The גמרא then asks why the משנה lists each case. It explains that every case rules out a different suspicion, such as the idea that the husband only meant to upset his wife. Next, a ברייתא teaches which words cancel a גט, and the גמרא challenges it from a ruling about a gift, where the word בטל means 'void from the start.' אביי begins his answer, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Heavy rain loosens a hoe's handle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the word יפרי as 'loosening': in heavy rain, even the handle stuck into the hole of a hoe becomes loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: The handle in the hole of the hoe becomes loose.
steps.whatsHappening: We join the end of a discussion from the previous page. The word יפרי is being explained as meaning that heavy rain loosens things, and the first example is a hoe's handle coming loose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tool handle is jammed tightly into the metal head, so it normally does not move. Saying that the rain loosens even this shows how strong the rain is, and it proves that יפרי means separating things that were joined.

keyTerms.meaning: The hole or socket the handle goes into

phrases.english: The handle in the hole of the hoe becomes loose.
phrases.notes: This finishes explaining the word יפרי from just before: the rain is so strong it loosens things that were stuck tight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the word יפרי from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יפרי means the rain loosens things, so that even a hoe's handle comes loose in its socket.

steps.title: רב יוסף: even a peg in the wall loosens
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף goes further: the rain loosens even a peg hammered into a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Even the peg in the wall becomes loose.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a stronger example of how much the rain loosens things. Even a peg hammered into a wall comes loose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אפילו ('even') shows that this is a step up from the hoe. A peg driven into a wall is held even more firmly, so loosening it shows an even stronger rain.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Even the peg in the wall becomes loose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1 with a stronger example of loosening.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rain loosens even a peg fixed in a wall.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: even a reed in a basket loosens
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב goes further still: even a reed woven into a basket comes loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Even the reed in the basket becomes loose.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives the strongest example of all. Even a reed woven into a basket becomes loose in such rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third level of אפילו. A reed woven tightly into a basket is locked in by the weave, so if even that loosens, the rain is extremely powerful. This closes the discussion of יפרי.
steps.whatToRemember: The three examples (hoe handle, peg in a wall, reed in a basket) climb step by step. They all show that יפרי means heavy rain loosening things that were tightly joined.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Even the reed in the basket becomes loose.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, even stronger example after רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rain loosens even a reed woven into a basket.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל הגט
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק: 'We will return to you, כל הגט.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, כל הגט.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק. It closes פרק כל הגט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the chapter and expresses the hope of coming back to learn it again. A new פרק begins right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
Name of the פרק being finished

phrases.english: We will return to you, Kol HaGet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion in steps 1 to 3.

steps.title: A husband can cancel a גט by telling the agent
steps.stepSummary: A new פרק opens. If a husband sent a גט with a שליח and then caught up to him, or sent a second שליח after him, and said 'the גט I gave you is cancelled', it is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sends a bill of divorce to his wife, and he reached the agent, or he sent an agent after him, and he said to him: 'The bill of divorce that I gave you, it is void', it is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The new משנה of פרק השולח begins. It rules that a husband can cancel the גט while it is still with the שליח, either by speaking to the שליח himself or through a second שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שליח only carries the גט for the husband, so the husband can still change his mind before the divorce happens. He can tell the שליח in person, or send another messenger to tell him. Either way, the גט becomes בטל.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sends (also the name of this new פרק)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different שליחים here. The first one carries the גט. The second one is only sent to tell the first one that the גט is cancelled.

phrases.english: One who sends a bill of divorce to his wife,
and he reached the agent,
or he sent an agent after him,
and he said to him:
'The bill of divorce that I gave you, it is void,'
it is void.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק with a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband can cancel a גט that is still with the שליח, by telling the שליח himself or through a second שליח.

steps.title: A husband can cancel a גט by telling the wife first
steps.stepSummary: If the husband got to his wife before the גט did, or sent a שליח to her, and said 'the גט I sent you is cancelled', it is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he went ahead to his wife or sent an agent to her, and said to her: 'The bill of divorce that I sent you, it is void', it is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second way to cancel. The husband tells the wife herself, in person or through a שליח, before the גט arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 5, but now the message goes to the wife instead of the carrying שליח. What matters is that the cancellation comes before the גט reaches her.

keyTerms.meaning: He went ahead, got there first

phrases.english: If he went ahead to his wife
phrases.notes: He reached her before the שליח with the גט did.

phrases.english: or he sent an agent to her,
and he said to her:
'The bill of divorce that I sent to you, it is void,'
it is void.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to step 5: the cancellation is told to the wife instead of the שליח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Telling the wife, directly or through a שליח, that the גט is cancelled before it reaches her makes it void.

steps.title: Once the גט reaches her hand, it can't be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The limit: once the גט has reached the wife's hand, the husband can no longer cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was once the bill of divorce reached her hand, he can no longer cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets the cutoff point for cancelling. As soon as the גט is in her hand, it is too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5 and 6 work because the divorce has not happened yet. When the גט reaches her hand, the divorce takes effect and she is divorced, so there is nothing left to cancel.
steps.whatToRemember: A husband can cancel a גט at any point before it reaches the wife's hand, whether he tells the שליח or the wife. Once it is in her hand, it is final.

phrases.english: If it was once the bill of divorce reached her hand,
he can no longer cancel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the time limit for the cancellations described in steps 5 and 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the גט reaches the wife's hand, the husband cannot cancel it.

steps.title: The old practice: cancelling before a בית דין elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: In earlier times, a husband could gather a בית דין in another place and cancel the גט there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Originally, he would convene a court in another place and cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how things used to work. The husband would cancel the גט before a בית דין somewhere else, without telling the שליח or the wife. This sets up the תקנה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike steps 5 and 6, here the cancellation happens far away. Neither the שליח nor the wife hears about it. This is a new method of cancelling, and it is what the next step deals with.

phrases.english: Originally, he would convene a court
in another place and cancel it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from cancellation told to the שליח or the wife to cancellation done elsewhere, before a בית דין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In earlier times, a husband could cancel a גט before a בית דין in a different place.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל הזקן stops the practice for תיקון העולם
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל הזקן enacted that people should no longer cancel a גט this way, מפני תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל the Elder instituted that they should not do so, for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל הזקן made a תקנה forbidding the old practice of cancelling the גט before a far-off בית דין. The reason given is תיקון העולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, cancelling elsewhere worked. Now a rabbinic enactment blocks that method, while cancelling by telling the שליח or the wife still works. The משנה names the reason, תיקון העולם, but does not spell it out here.

keyTerms.meaning: The betterment of the world, a reason for a rabbinic enactment

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the well-known תקנות made מפני תיקון העולם. It shows that the חכמים set limits on how a גט may be cancelled.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted
that they should not do so,
for the betterment of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Forbids the old practice described in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the תקנה of רבן גמליאל הזקן, a husband may no longer cancel a גט before a בית דין in another place.

steps.title: Even a chance meeting with the שליח lets the husband cancel the גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה says 'הגיע' (he reached), not 'הגיעו' (he chased him down). So even if the husband ran into the שליח by chance, his cancellation works, and we do not say he only meant to upset his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה does not say 'he caught up with him.' It says 'he reached.' That means even if they met by chance. And we do not say he only meant to cause her distress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה by looking closely at one word. That word shows the cancellation works even if the husband met the שליח by accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הגיעו' would mean he actively chased the שליח, which shows he truly wants to cancel. 'הגיע' includes a chance meeting, where one might suspect he is just saying 'cancelled' to stall and upset his wife. The משנה's wording teaches that we take his words seriously anyway, and the גט is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה
He caught up with him (actively chased the שליח)
He reached (any meeting, even by chance)
By itself, by chance, without effort
To cause her distress, to vex her

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether he has the power to cancel. The worry is whether he really means it, or is only saying it to upset his wife. The גמרא says we accept his words as a real cancellation.

phrases.english: Gemara
It does not teach 'he reached him,'
phrases.notes: 'הגיעו' would mean he went after the שליח on purpose and caught him.

phrases.english: but rather 'he reached' —
and that includes even by chance,
and we do not say
that he only intends to cause her distress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's first case (step 5) by reading its exact wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband's cancellation works even if he met the שליח by chance; we do not assume he only meant to vex his wife.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the case of a second שליח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothers to say the husband can cancel by sending a second שליח after the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or he sent a שליח after him.' Why do I need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this case is in the משנה, since it seems obvious. The next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's שליח stands in his place. So if the husband can cancel in person, it seems obvious that a שליח he sends can cancel for him. The גמרא wants to know what new lesson this case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this? (asks why a line seems unnecessary)
After him, chasing the first שליח

phrases.english: 'Or he sent a messenger after him' —
why do I need this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁלַח אַחֲרָיו שָׁלִיחַ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second case in the משנה's first clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does the case of a second שליח teach, if it seems obvious?

steps.title: A second שליח is strong enough to cancel the first שליח's mission
steps.stepSummary: You might have thought one שליח's mission is no stronger than another's, so the second cannot undo the first. The משנה teaches that he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the second שליח's mission is no stronger than the first שליח's mission, so it cannot cancel it. So the משנה teaches us that it can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing the mistake the משנה is preventing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both messengers were sent by the same husband, so one might think they are equals and the later one cannot undo the earlier one. The משנה teaches that the later instruction wins, because the second שליח carries the husband's newest wish.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought... (sets up a mistaken idea)
The mission or authority of a שליח
The later one / the earlier one

phrases.english: You might have said:
the mission of the later messenger is not stronger
than the mission of the earlier one, such that it could cancel it,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without this case one might think two messengers are equal and the second cannot cancel the first; the משנה teaches that he can.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the case of the husband reaching his wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say the husband can cancel by getting to his wife before the גט does.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He got to his wife first.' Why do I need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the next case in the משנה (step 6). The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that the husband's cancellation works when he tells the שליח. Telling his wife directly seems just as good, so the case looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: He got there first, before the גט

phrases.english: 'He got to his wife first' —
why do I need this?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדַם הוּא אֵצֶל אִשְׁתּוֹ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the משנה's second clause (step 6).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does the case of the husband reaching his wife teach?

steps.title: Even when he tells his wife directly, we do not assume he only wants to upset her
steps.stepSummary: You might have thought that we trust him only when he tells the שליח, but when he tells his wife directly he surely just wants to hurt her. The משנה teaches that the cancellation works here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: when we do not say 'he only wants to upset her,' that is only when he speaks to the שליח. But when he speaks to her, he surely only wants to upset her. So the משנה teaches us that the cancellation works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this case rules out the suspicion that a husband talking to his wife is only trying to hurt her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 taught that we do not suspect him of only trying to upset her when he tells the שליח. Telling the wife herself 'your גט is cancelled' looks even more like an attempt to upset her. The משנה teaches that even then we accept his words and the גט is cancelled.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא אָמְרִינַן לְצַעוֹרַהּ קָא מִיכַּוֵּין –
phrases.english: when we do not say that he intends to cause her distress —
phrases.notes: This points back to step 10, where we did not suspect him of only trying to upset her.

phrases.english: that applies only when he speaks to the messenger,
but when he speaks to her herself,
he certainly intends to cause her distress,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא כִּי לָא אָמְרִינַן לְצַעוֹרַהּ קָא מִיכַּוֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13, building on the idea of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without this case one might think speaking directly to the wife is surely only to upset her; the משנה teaches the cancellation still works.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the case of a שליח sent to the wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה adds that the husband can cancel by sending a שליח to his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or he sent a שליח to her.' Why do I need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the last case in this part of the משנה. The answer is in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband can tell his wife himself, a שליח who stands in his place should obviously be able to do the same. So this case seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: To her (the wife), not after the first שליח
A שליח sent to the wife, unlike a שליח sent after the first שליח (אַחֲרָיו)

phrases.english: 'Or he sent a messenger to her' —
why do I need this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁלַח אֶצְלָהּ שָׁלִיחַ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second case of the משנה's second clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does the case of a שליח sent to the wife teach?

steps.title: A שליח sent to the wife also cancels the גט, even though the husband loses no effort
steps.stepSummary: You might have thought a husband would not go to the trouble himself just to upset her, but he might easily send someone else, since that trouble costs him nothing. The משנה teaches that the cancellation works here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: he himself would not go to the trouble just to upset her. But a שליח, whose trouble he does not care about, he surely sends only to upset her. So the משנה teaches us that the cancellation works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last question. Sending a שליח to the wife is also a real cancellation, not just a way to upset her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband goes himself, his effort shows he is serious. When he sends someone else, the effort is not his, so one might suspect he is only trying to upset her. The משנה teaches that we still accept it as a real cancellation.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes the trouble, makes an effort

steps.whatToRemember: Every way the husband cancels before the גט reaches her works: chasing the שליח or meeting him by chance, sending a second שליח, telling his wife, or sending a שליח to her. In each case we do not say he only meant to upset her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה lists so many similar cases. Each one rules out a different reason to think the cancellation might not count.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is he himself who would not take the trouble
just to cause her distress,
but a messenger,
since the husband does not care if he takes the trouble —
phrases.notes: The trouble belongs to the שליח, not the husband, so it costs the husband nothing.

phrases.english: he certainly intends to cause her distress,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא אִיהוּ הוּא דְּלָא טָרַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 and completes the series of 'למה לי' questions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without this case one might think sending a שליח costs the husband nothing and is only meant to upset her; the משנה teaches the cancellation still works.

steps.title: Once the גט reaches her, he cannot cancel it. Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the last clause of the משנה and asks why it needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if the גט already reached her hand, he cannot cancel it. The גמרא asks: that's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's final rule, that after the גט reaches the wife the husband can no longer cancel it, and asks why such an obvious point needs saying. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wife receives the גט, she is divorced. A divorce that already happened cannot be undone, so the rule seems too simple to need a teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: once it reached her hand (she received it)

phrases.english: But if after the get reached her hand —
he cannot cancel it.
That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'why does the משנה need to say this' questions about each clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה needs to state that the husband cannot cancel after the גט reaches her.

steps.title: Even if he was chasing the messenger the whole time, it is too late
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a husband who was running after the שליח from the start to cancel, but only caught up after the גט was delivered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed where he was chasing after it from the start in order to cancel it. You might have said that this shows he really cancelled it all along. The משנה teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case: the husband set out to cancel before the גט was delivered, but he arrived too late. The משנה teaches that the גט still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might have thought his early effort proves he cancelled it in his heart before delivery, so the cancellation should count looking back. The משנה teaches that a cancellation only works if it is actually said before the גט reaches her. Intention and chasing are not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for this case

steps.whatToRemember: A husband can cancel a גט only until it reaches his wife's hand. After that, even if he was on his way to cancel it all along, it is too late.

phrases.english: It is needed only
where he was chasing after it from the beginning in order to cancel it;
phrases.notes: He set out after the שליח before the גט was delivered, but caught up only after.

phrases.english: you might have said:
the matter is revealed looking back
that he really did cancel it,
so it teaches us that he did not.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דְּמַהְדַּר עֲלֵיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא לְבַטּוֹלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question by giving a case where the rule is not obvious.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a husband who was chasing the שליח to cancel but arrived after delivery. The גט still stands.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His chase proves he cancelled it before delivery, so it is void looking back.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a cancellation actually made before the גט reaches her counts.

steps.title: Which words cancel a גט and which do nothing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that 'it is void' or 'I don't want it' cancels the גט, while 'it is invalid' or 'it is not a גט' does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if the husband says 'It is void' or 'I don't want it,' his words take effect. If he says 'It is invalid' or 'It is not a גט,' he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing which statements by the husband cancel a גט he sent and which do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'It is void' and 'I don't want it' are real acts of cancelling, so they work. 'It is invalid' and 'It is not a גט' are claims that something was wrong with the גט all along. Since the גט really has no flaw, these false claims do nothing.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he said 'It is void';
or 'I don't want it' —
his words take effect.
If he said 'It is invalid' or 'It is not a get' —
he said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the wording a husband must use to cancel a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בטל הוא' and 'אי אפשי בו' cancel the גט. 'פסול הוא' and 'אינו גט' have no effect.

steps.title: In the case of a gift, 'void' means void from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from a ruling about gifts, where 'it is void' is treated as a claim about the past.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean 'void' means 'let it become void'? But רבה בר איבו said in the name of רב ששת (some say רבה בר אבוה said): someone who received a gift and then said 'This gift is cancelled,' 'Let it be cancelled,' or 'I don't want it' said nothing. If he said 'It is void' or 'It is not a gift,' his words take effect. So 'void' means void from the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. The ברייתא treats בטל as a cancelling word for the future, but a ruling about gifts treats the same word as meaning 'void from the start.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a gift reaches the receiver, he owns it and cannot cancel it going forward. So 'it is void' can only work there if it means 'I never accepted it in the first place.' But if בטל means 'from the beginning,' then for a גט it should be just like 'it is not a גט' and do nothing. Yet the ברייתא says it works.

keyTerms.meaning: let it become void (from now on)

steps.confusionAlert: The same word בטל gives opposite results in the two cases. In the gift case 'void' works and 'let it be cancelled' doesn't. For the גט, 'void' works but 'it is not a גט' doesn't. The question is what the word itself means.

phrases.english: Is this to say that 'void'
is wording that means 'let it become void'?!
But didn't Rabba bar Aivu say
that Rav Sheshet said;

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: and some say Rabba bar Avuh said:
One who receives a gift
and said, after the gift came into his hand:
'This gift is cancelled';
'Let it be cancelled'; 'I don't want it' —
he said nothing.
'It is void'; 'It is not a gift' —
phrases.notes: These mean he never agreed to take the gift at all, so it was never his.

phrases.english: his words take effect.
So 'void' means void from the beginning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's assumption about what בטל means.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that 'בטל הוא' works as a cancellation of a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The gift ruling shows בטל means 'void from the beginning.' If so, for a גט it should be a false claim about the past, like 'אינו גט,' and have no effect.

steps.title: אביי begins his answer about the word 'void'
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to answer the contradiction about the meaning of בטל. His answer continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'Void'...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to answer the contradiction between the ברייתא about the גט and the ruling about the gift. Only his opening word appears here, and his explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is about to explain how בטל can be understood in a way that fits both rulings. Keep the question from the last step in mind while reading his answer.

phrases.english: Abaye said: 'Void'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the response to the contradiction raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarification of the word בטל (answer continues)
